targets.title: Intonation and auditory grouping in immediate serial recall.
targets.evidence_quote: To this aim, we replicated Frankish’s ( 1995 ) serial recall experiment using natural stimuli with pitch contours conveying positional information.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results differ from those obtained by Frankish ( 1995 ), possibly for two reasons: (1) In our stimuli, we use a natural (pre-recorded) voice instead of synthesized speech, and (2) unlike English, Italian words for digits are mostly disyllabic, allowing for more time for the intonation contour to unfold, making them better able to lend salience to the digit if a rise is used.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly differ from original null intonation finding; a positive new effect contradicts that original.

reasoning: Explicit conceptual replication of Frankish (1995) with natural Italian stimuli and a fresh participant sample. Saito supplies background on the same claim; modality studies motivate the added manipulation but are not identified as the experiment replicated.
